_purpose: The SECOND trust layer (Gate 4N-I28W, closing I28V-02). It protects the assertion-control mechanism itself, which the primary registry cannot do without validating itself.
_trust_boundary: LAYER 1 — tests/fixtures/assertion-contract-registry.json states what each load-bearing TEST
LAYER 2 — this file states what the CONTROL ITSELF must do, and which mandatory tests must be
collected and must run. scripts/assertion_contracts.py::validate_meta checks it.
The two layers are deliberately separate files with separate entry points so neither can
silently remove its own protection: weakening layer 1 is caught by layer 2, and weakening
layer 2 is caught by the layer-2 test being itself listed as mandatory in layer 2.
HONEST LIMIT. This is not protection against a party able to rewrite every independent source
in one change. An authored oracle cannot prove itself universally, and this file does not
claim to. What it does is make each weakening require a separate, visible, reviewable edit in
a different file from the one being weakened.

required_validator_behaviours.requirement: a missing registry is refused, never defaulted to empty
an unknown assertion class in a contract is refused
required_validator_behaviours.probe: a contract naming a class outside ASSERTION_CLASSES

required_validator_behaviours.requirement: an assertion that cannot execute cannot satisfy a required class
required_validator_behaviours.probe: a contracted assertion wrapped in `if False:`

required_validator_behaviours.requirement: an always-true assertion cannot satisfy a required class
a required class must be present with its stable references
an unregistered helper used as the assertion mechanism is refused
a contracted test that no longer exists is a problem, not a skip
a contracted file absent from the tree is a problem
required_validator_behaviours.probe: a contract pointing at a nonexistent file

required_validator_behaviours.requirement: a file that does not parse is a problem and is never skipped
the CLI exits non-zero when any problem is reported
required_validator_behaviours.probe: run the CLI against a registry with a known problem

mandatory_tests.why: the primary assertion-contract control; if it is removed, renamed or deselected, no contracted assertion is checked at all
the layer-2 control; listing it here is what stops layer 2 from being removed silently
the collection pin itself; without it, deselection or renaming of any mandatory test would go unnoticed

pytest.raises.failure_semantics: fails when the expected exception is NOT raised inside the context
pytest.raises.implementation_note: provided by pytest, outside this repository; there is no in-tree implementation that could be weakened. If a PROJECT helper is ever registered, implementation_source must become in_tree and implementation_sha256 must pin it.

pytest.fail.implementation_note: provided by pytest, outside this repository; there is no in-tree implementation that could be weakened. If a PROJECT helper is ever registered, implementation_source must become in_tree and implementation_sha256 must pin it.

pytest.approx.failure_semantics: not an assertion by itself; only meaningful inside a comparison
pytest.approx.implementation_note: provided by pytest, outside this repository; there is no in-tree implementation that could be weakened. If a PROJECT helper is ever registered, implementation_source must become in_tree and implementation_sha256 must pin it.

_helper_implementation_rule: A registered helper is either third_party (no in-tree implementation, so its semantics cannot be
weakened from inside this repository) or in_tree, in which case it MUST carry an
implementation_sha256 that validate_meta verifies. Registering a project helper without pinning
its implementation is a problem, not an omission — that is the only way 'the helper's
implementation was weakened' can be detected rather than assumed away.
